Define the proposed gate explicitly: gₜˡ = sigmoid(Aˡeₜ + Bˡhₜ₋₁ˡ + bˡ), then hₜˡ = GRUCellˡ(xₜˡ, gₜˡ ⊙ hₜ₋₁ˡ). Feed the current item embedding eₜ directly into every layer’s gate; upper-layer GRU inputs still come from the preceding layer. This is a proposed ablation design, not an established improvement. Compare the corrected baseline, a custom-cell control with g≡1, and learned gating; optionally remove direct embedding conditioning separately. Copy baseline weights into the identity control and verify evaluation-mode equivalence. For left padding, freeze every layer’s state on padding steps and read the final nonpadding position, never count−1.

Preserve embedding/interlayer/output dropout locations, probabilities and mask semantics, plus loss reduction, valid-target masking, negative sampling, optimizer and initialization. PyTorch applies built-in GRU dropout between layers, excluding the last; its reset-gate equation also differs from some original GRU formulations, so custom cells must reproduce the actual baseline algebra. [PyTorch GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html). A timestep loop around GRUCell can sacrifice fused sequence throughput; measure synchronized training-step time, examples/second and peak memory on representative batches, including backward passes. Report accuracy at matched update counts alongside GPU-seconds; do not assume equal epochs imply equal cost.

Using each category’s single selected checkpoint in evaluation mode, measure gate means, quantiles, fractions below 0.05/above 0.95, and retained-state norm ratios by layer and history-length bin, excluding padding. Report bin counts and validation HR@10 alongside macro HR@10 across all four categories; saturation alone does not establish useful retention. Keep preprocessing/training seeds 0/42, fixed sampling/evaluation, 200-epoch maximum and 200 batches/epoch. Maintain predictor/checkpoint and diagnostic-interface consistency; budget every ablation, with no checkpoint averaging or score fusion.
